facts.what: The Leibholz-Schmul marriage at Schubin, akt nr 9 of 1874
facts.why: Published as 24 November from 22 September, with the claim that the family record's date 'now stands on the register itself'. It does not. The entry reads 'Schubin am 24 vier und zwanzigsten December'. Corroborated by akt nr 8, which is also December in the same hand, and by akt nr 7, which really is 24 November - the near-miss that confirmed the expected date before the right entry was opened.

facts.what: The given name of Sally Leibholz's mother in the same entry
facts.now: H-- geb. Pollnow, the rest of the word unreadable
facts.why: Read as Wilhelmine on 22 September and as Philipine by the portal's volunteer indexer. Both fall. The clerk's capital P, four words along the same line in POLLNOW, is a single round bowl and the disputed capital has none; his capital H in HAMMERSTEIN has a flat baseline lead-in, two steep diagonals and a low crossbar, and the disputed capital has all three; and his capital W in WENGATZ on akt nr 8 is two rounded looping arches, which it plainly is not.

facts.what: How Kurt Israel Luwinski's paternity of Derrick is characterised
facts.now: Excluded as biological father — settled. Father of record and of upbringing. Who the biological father was is the open question.
facts.why: The exclusion is not a dispute and is not open: 0.0% Ashkenazi where a quarter would be required, and a Y haplogroup, R-S11477, that is North Sea rather than Ashkenazi. The tree page grades him 'ruled out' and says explicitly that this is not a level on the evidence ladder but a claim tested and failed. What is open is WHO the biological father was. The phrase 'disputed by DNA' survived on derrick.astro's summary panel for a fortnight after the exclusion was published, was copied from there into a chart note by a peer session building charts, and so the page argued with itself within one screen. IT WAS TRUE WHEN WRITTEN AND WAS NEVER READ AGAINST THE FINDING THAT REPLACED IT.

facts.what: Where Jeannett (E M) Wear was living at 18 Ridge Avenue, Letchworth on 29 September 1939
facts.now: In the family's own house, alone, after the rest had sailed
was: in lodgings half a mile off on Ridge Avenue
facts.why: The word 'lodgings' was never in a record. The archive had 18 Ridge Avenue only from the 1939 Register, which gives an address and not a tenure, and filled the gap with an assumption because the family's known house was 72 Pix Road. The BT 27 passenger lists settle it: column 6, 'Last Address in the United Kingdom', reads 18 Ridge Ave, Letchworth for Henry Robert on the Durban Castle of 5 April 1939 AND for Martha Maud and the four youngest on the Dunvegan Castle of 10 August 1939. It was the family home. She had not moved out.

facts.what: What the Schoeneberg II marriage entry of 5 January 1924 would contain
facts.now: It names NO parents. The 1920s Prussian form cites each party's birth register instead.
was: A MARRIAGE ENTRY NAMES BOTH SETS OF PARENTS
a German marriage register entry names THE PARENTS OF BOTH PARTIES
a German marriage entry names the parents of both parties
facts.why: Predicted on 20 September from the index alone, on the strength of the pre-1920 form, and published as what the certificate 'will contain'. The entry arrived from the Landesarchiv on 29 September and gives, for each party, name, how identity was established, date and place of birth, BIRTH REGISTER NUMBER AND OFFICE, and residence. No parents. Joachim Luwinski, Johanna nee Thimm, Sally Leibholz and Friederike nee Schmul remain unconfirmed on a single document. Second time in one day a row here was planned around a field the relevant form revision does not have; the other was BT 27. NOTE ON THE STRING ITSELF: the first withdrawal listed 'names the parents of both parties', which flagged two statements that are TRUE about other documents — the 1874 Schubin entry, whose form does name them, and a 1940 Johannesburg certificate. A withdrawn value has to be specific to the claim, not to the sentence pattern, or the gate starts refusing correct work. Narrowed twice: 'BOTH SETS OF PARENTS' on its own is TRUE of the 1874 Prussian form, which this archive has read and proved - Jacob the elder and a mother nee Pollnow, Juda Schmul and Jutta nee Machol, all four off one 1874 entry. The form of 1874 names parents; the form of 1924 does not. THE WITHDRAWN THING IS THE GENERALISATION, NOT THE SENTENCE.
